content.text: No Customer-payable liquidated damages exist. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 14.3 Liquidated Damages. In the event that Array (a) [ * ] during [ * ], or (b) intentionally conceals or falsifies a material result and/or material item of data concerning the safety or efficacy of the Product ... then, as an alternative to its right to terminate this Agreement pursuant to Section 13.3 above, Ono may in its discretion elect to continue this Agreement, in which case (A) Ono shall be relieved of its due diligence obligations under this Agreement; and (B) as liquidated damages for the breaches described
input.rationale: The only liquidated-damages provision (Section 14.3) runs entirely in our favour: it is triggered by Array's breach or concealment/falsification of safety or efficacy data, relieves Ono of its diligence obligations, and reduces the otherwise applicable royalty rate as liquidated damages (p0671). Liquidated damages payable by the Vendor to the Customer are expressly compliant under this rule, so no redline. We found no Customer-payable penalty, minimum fee on termination, or early-termination fee anywhere in the Agreement: Article XIV imposes only transition/wind-down obligations, and the only other payment-default mechanic is the mutual late-payment interest in Section 7.1 (LIBOR/interbank plus a margin), which is a commercial interest rate rather than a penalty and therefore not a liquidated-damages deviation. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer).
